clue.text: Woman going round edges of county on rear of fast harvester

indicators.note: the woman's word goes round the outside of the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman

indicators.note: edges of county asks for that word's first and last letters only
rear of fast asks for the final letter of that word

explanation.surface: A woman drives round the borders of a county on the back of a speedy combine harvester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harvester' suggests a machine or a farmhand; it is the hand tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A scythe is the long curved blade traditionally used to cut grain, so it is a harvesting implement.

clue.text: Copper hauled up sailor with second weapon

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: in a down clue, hauled up means the sailor's word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor

explanation.surface: A policeman drags a sailor and an accomplice upward along with a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hauled up' turns SALT into TLAS in this down entry; 'Copper' is the element, not a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword once carried by sailors, so it is a weapon.

clue.text: Legal period some barrister mentioned

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A barrister refers in passing to a length of time in law.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'barrisTER Mentioned'.
explanation.definitionFit: Law courts and Inns of Court sit in terms, named sittings of the legal year, so a term is a legal period.

clue.text: Early assessment of crossing places?

parts.note: crossing here means marking a cross on a ballot paper, and the places are where people vote; the survey is taken as they leave, before the official count

explanation.surface: A preliminary survey of road junctions or pedestrian crossings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing places' suggests junctions; it means polling stations, where voters put a cross on the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters questioned as they leave polling stations give the earliest estimate of an election result.

clue.text: Put down to slip out of shot?

definitions.meaning: to put down a ruler is to remove them from power
to stop holding the pose struck for a photograph

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the word as DE (out of) plus POSE, the posture held for a camera shot.
explanation.definitionFit: To depose a monarch is to put them down from the throne; jokily, to drop a photographic pose.

clue.text: Boring formality? It produces obscurity

parts.note: something dry is dull or boring
ice is cold reserve or stiff formality of manner

explanation.surface: A dull, stiff ceremony leaves everyone in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: Frozen carbon dioxide is used on stage to make a low fog, which obscures the view.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid carbon dioxide gives off dense white vapour, the theatrical fog that hides the stage.

clue.text: An element of theatricality?

parts.note: a metallic chemical element that shares its name with a famous London theatre

explanation.walkthrough: The London Palladium is a celebrated West End variety theatre; the same name is the metal with symbol Pd.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a platinum-group metal and a theatre, so it is literally an element tied to theatre.

clue.text: Gull, say, doing for airbeds

indicators.note: doing for means ruining or wrecking, so the letters of airbeds are destroyed and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A gull sets about destroying some inflatable mattresses on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing for' is the anagram signal (to do for is to wreck); 'say' marks the gull as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A gull is one example of a bird that lives by the sea.

clue.text: You can stop for a while now, sire

definitions.text: You can stop for a while now, sire

parts.words: You can stop for a while now, sire
parts.note: sire is read as a new father, not a king, given permission to take time off work after the birth

explanation.surface: A courtier tells the king he may take a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sire' looks like a form of address to a monarch; here it is a verb-made noun: one who has fathered a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Time off work granted to a new father after his baby is born fits the permission given to the sire.

clue.text: Campaigning aggressively employs its grammar ultimately

indicators.note: aggressively says the letters are attacked and thrown about into a new order

parts.note: used as written as part of the letters to be mixed

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of grammar

explanation.surface: A campaign of aggressive pedantry makes use of correct grammar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aggressively' mixes EMPLOYSITS with R (the last letter of 'grammar', from 'ultimately'); 'Campaigning' is the noun sense, the act of campaigning.
explanation.definitionFit: Proselytism is active effort to win converts to a belief, a form of campaigning.

clue.text: See 8
Postal order coming in unusually behindhand — allow extension

indicators.note: coming in says the postal order's letters enter between the other pieces

parts.note: extra means unusually, as in extra large
behindhand means late or behind schedule

explanation.surface: A postal order arriving very late lets someone have more time to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extension' suggests more time on a deadline; it means projecting a trend beyond the known data.
explanation.definitionFit: To extrapolate is to extend known figures or trends beyond the range observed.

clue.text: TV relay linked to a new town in Scotland

parts.note: OB stands for outside broadcast, a television relay from a location

explanation.surface: A television transmission connected to a newly built Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: OBAN is a port town on Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a ferry port on the west coast of Scotland, in Argyll.

clue.text: Expert finding phosphorus in decomposed silicates

indicators.note: in places the phosphorus symbol inside the rearranged letters
decomposed means broken down, so the letters of silicates are taken apart and reassembled

parts.note: P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

explanation.surface: A chemist identifies phosphorus among broken-down silicate minerals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decomposed' turns SILICATES into SECIALIST and 'in' puts P inside it after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist is someone with expert knowledge of a particular field.

clue.text: Three bridge players almost sign for group

parts.note: the four bridge players are named by compass points, and East, North and South give three of them

indicators.note: almost means the sign's word loses its last letter

parts.note: an emblem is a sign or symbol

explanation.surface: Three people at a bridge table nearly signal to a group.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players sit as North, South, East and West; 'almost' drops the final M from EMBLEM.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensemble is a group of performers or things considered together.

clue.text: Unusually moral clue about particles

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of moral clue appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An odd moral lesson concerns tiny particles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about particles' is the definition: the answer describes things relating to molecules.
explanation.definitionFit: Molecular means relating to molecules, the tiny particles of a substance.

clue.text: State what's to be found in the main diagonal

indicators.note: what's to be found in says the answer lies concealed inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Name what lies along the leading diagonal of a matrix.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'maIN DIAgonal'; 'State' is a country, not a verb meaning say.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a country, and a nation is a state.

clue.text: Description of dove? Real upset during description of war

indicators.note: during says one piece sits within the other, the way an event falls within a period

parts.note: the Cold War gives cold as a description of a war

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of real are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: Turmoil within a war gives a picture of a peace symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: The collared dove is a common bird named for the dark ring on its neck; the Cold War supplies 'description of war'.
explanation.definitionFit: The collared dove is a species with a black half-ring on its neck, so collared describes it.

clue.text: Restraint long deployed by countryman

parts.note: a yoke is a wooden restraint across the necks of draught animals
L is the abbreviation for long, as in garment sizes

explanation.surface: A farmhand puts a long harness to use.
explanation.definitionFit: A yokel is an unsophisticated person from the countryside.

clue.text: Family work in US company's realm

parts.note: kin are one's family or relatives

indicators.note: in places the work's word inside the company's letters

parts.note: GM is General Motors, the American car company
to do is to work or perform

explanation.surface: Relatives working for an American firm.
explanation.walkthrough: GM is General Motors, the American car maker, signalled by 'US company'.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingdom is a realm ruled by a monarch.

clue.text: Soldier joining company to suffice here?

definitions.text: Soldier joining company to suffice here?

indicators.note: joining says the soldier's word comes next to the company's, side by side

parts.note: com is short for company, as in a dotcom firm
a man is an ordinary soldier, as in officers and men
to do means to be enough, as in that will do

explanation.surface: A soldier joins a unit to make up its numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole the clue describes a soldier signing up with an elite company; the pieces COM, MAN and DO build the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a soldier in an elite assault unit, the kind who joins a company for special raids.

clue.text: See, in Narnia, possibly, a peaceful state

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for see inside the rearranged letters
possibly says the letters of Narnia may be arranged another way

parts.note: v stands for vide, Latin for see, used in references

explanation.surface: Look, the magical land of Narnia might be a place of tranquillity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns NARNIA into NIRANA and 'in' puts V inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana in Buddhism is a state of perfect peace free from desire and suffering.

clue.text: I am suppressing name following years in bad odour

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down, so the I am letters close over and contain the others

parts.note: f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Keeping a name quiet after years of disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppressing' puts N and F inside I AM; 'in bad odour' is an idiom for being in disgrace, so 'bad odour' means disrepute.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in bad odour is to be in disfavour, and infamy is public disgrace or notoriety.

clue.text: Badly annoy client, sending one off without thinking

indicators.note: badly says the letters are put together in a poor, jumbled order
sending off means dismissing, so the letter for one is removed
sending off means dismissing, so the letter for one is removed

parts.note: a is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A shop assistant irritates a customer and has someone ejected without a second thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sending one off' removes A from ANNOYCLIENT; 'Badly' mixes the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something innocently means doing it naively, without guile or forethought.

clue.text: Variations will conceal tune

indicators.note: will conceal says the answer lies inside the word variations

explanation.surface: Musical variations will disguise the melody.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside 'vARIAtions'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a song for solo voice in an opera, a tune.

clue.text: Cuts off rising politico-speak

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: nips means cuts off, as in nipping off a bud

explanation.surface: Politicians' jargon is cut off as it grows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reads NIPS upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Spin is the slanted presentation of news by political press officers.

clue.text: Sunderland kit desired by little boys?

definitions.text: Sunderland kit desired by little boys?

parts.words: Sunderland kit desired by little boys?
parts.note: the Short Sunderland was a wartime flying boat, so its kit is a build-your-own scale replica, a favourite of young boys

explanation.walkthrough: Sunderland suggests the football club and its strip; it is the Short Sunderland flying boat, sold as a plastic construction kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A plastic construction kit of the Sunderland flying boat builds a scale replica of the aircraft.

clue.text: See 25
Crawling Sergeant Major leading troops

indicators.note: leading says the sergeant major's letters go at the front, ahead of the troops

parts.note: an army is a body of troops

explanation.surface: A sergeant major at the head of his soldiers is sucking up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crawling' looks like movement on all fours; it means sucking up to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Crawling means fawning or obsequious, and smarmy describes an oily, ingratiating manner.

clue.text: Agreement about Northern Ireland? No

indicators.note: about means around, so the agreement's word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a deal is an agreement

explanation.surface: An agreement concerning Northern Ireland is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' is the definition: a denial is a refusal or saying no.
explanation.definitionFit: A denial is a refusal or contradiction, the act of saying no.
